blind_comparisons.question: Which timeline shows a player whose invulnerability is AIMED at the enemy weapon rather than sprayed near it?
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: In B every invulnerability run sits directly under an enemy hitbox column and there are no invulnerable runs standing alone for the first two thirds of the strip. In A there are invulnerable runs with no enemy hitbox beneath them (columns ~10-12, ~57-58, ~104-110, ~140-142) and, worse, a long tail of bare enemy hitbox columns with no invulnerability anywhere near them. A is a player rolling on a rhythm; B is a player rolling at something.

blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: Round 1 established that our H[k] i-frame vector and one generated from §B are bit-identical in all four tiers, and my re-run of critic-iframe.json on this build is byte-identical to round 1's file, so the pack is still degenerate. Filed as a corpus extension.
Same degeneracy: the 14-row census is bit-identical to §A/§B.

Round 1 ran this pack and the pick landed on the reference. The stamina economy has since changed materially (M7 now passes 7 of 7 rows) so round 1's result does not transfer; re-running it was not reached in this session and is recorded rather than claimed.
The pack is two hyperarmour probe vectors S[k] and two backstab fields. Our hyperarmour probe is vacuous — its control case takes zero damage — so there is no S[k] to put in a pack.
The pack is two M4 64-row tables. Ours is exact against §B, so the two sides coincide — the same degeneracy as RI-CMB01 and RI-CMB02.
The pack is two per-move PWR tables. There is no enemy AI, so there is no per-move PWR distribution to tabulate — only one enemy's four scripted moves.

RI-CMB07 scores 0 on its own scale: M0 fails because the RI-AI01 §A enemy stream is absent, M1 cannot run because the item's own scenario fixture is invalidated, M2 is Mode B-prime rather than Mode B with four banded rows out, M3(d) does not cluster, M4 was not run.
RI-CMB02, RI-CMB05, RI-CMB06, RI-CMB09 and RI-CMB11 are all below their own we-lose floors.
The single biggest gap is a hit-geometry defect that lets a motionless player kill the piece's boss-class enemy without taking damage.

biggest_gap.what: An enemy attack's swept volume does not cover the attacker's own root translation, so it cannot hit a target standing inside its forward root travel. Measured on a stationary player against a stationary champion_hist_marked in arena_champion, sweeping 0.0-4.0 m in 0.1 m steps: the chop hits from 1.2 m to 3.6 m and misses at EVERY distance from 0.0 to 1.1 m; the thrust hits 1.6-4.0 m and misses 0.0-1.5 m; combo_a hits 1.1-2.9 m and misses 0.0-1.0 m. Those minimum distances are the attacks' declared root_dz_m of 1.2 / 1.6 / 0.9. Zeroing root_dz_m moves the inner boundary to 0.6 / 0.8 / 0.8 m, confirming the root translation is the cause (data file reverted, git clean). The player's own weapons have no such hole — dagger, straight sword, spear, greatsword and halberd all hit from 0.0 m. The consequence, measured: a player who stands completely still at 0.8-1.1 m and does nothing but mash the light attack kills the 2876-HP champion in 1153-1377 frames taking ZERO damage, while the enemy completes 44-54 frames of live hitbox and suffers zero stagger frames. This is also the mechanical cause of the exemplar's headline out-of-band row: 141 of 211 enemy swings resolve as WHIFF, and 35 swings across five fights had the player invulnerable for every active frame at 0.01-0.60 m — inside the hole, where the swing could not have connected anyway, so i-frame negation reads 0.111 against a band of 0.40-0.80.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The correct way to fight this game's boss is to walk inside it and stand still, which makes rolling, spacing, stamina and the entire i-frame system that RI-CMB01 gets exactly right decorative.

remedy.action: Sweep the attacker's root translation as well as its animated pose. RI-CMB04 §A's step order runs 5 (consume root motion) before 8 (sweep + query, this frame's pose vs last frame's); the sweep must interpolate the weapon socket capsule between last frame's WORLD-space pose and this frame's WORLD-space pose — root delta included — and the SUBSTEPS count must be derived from the larger of the arc travel and the root travel, not from the arc alone. A root_dz_m of 1.2 m spread over a 10-frame active window is 0.12 m per frame, which is inside one capsule radius, so the fix is a space change rather than a substep increase; verify both. Then re-derive SUBSTEPS from the measured maximum of (per-frame tip travel, per-frame root travel).
targets: game/src/combat (step 8 of RI-CMB04 §A's step order, the sweep + query stage)
game/data/combat/hitgeometry.json (the `sweep` block and its substep rationale)
tools/harness/critic-w1-09-r2.mjs --probe reach / --probe turtle (the acceptance instrument, already written)
remedy.acceptance: critic-r2-reach.json shows min_hit_distance_m <= 0.35 m for chop, thrust and combo_a with root_dz_m unchanged at 1.2 / 1.6 / 0.9, and no miss at any distance between 0.0 m and the attack's outer reach; AND critic-r2-turtle.json shows a motionless mashing player at 0.8, 1.0, 1.1 and 1.5 m taking >= 0.4 x max HP; AND the RI-CMB07 exemplar's row 11 (swings negated by i-frames) reaches 0.40-0.80 on the median of five fights with the enemy whiff share below 0.35.

secondary_observations.what: Row 9 of RI-CMB07 §D carries a band — 'all within [-24, +8]' — and the shipped statistics file computes its value and then sets band:null, in_band:null. Its measured values are [-8,17], [-9,15], [-10,15], [-7,15], [-8,13]: it is out of band in five fights of five, on the upper end, every time. It is the only row with a stated band that the file un-bands. Counted, the exemplar has four banded rows out of band, not three, and the denominator is 26 rather than 24. RI-CMB07's own text says '24 rows that carry a band' while §D shows 26, which is a corpus defect in its own right.

The exemplar's danger is a dial, not an emergent property. Each bot profile carries an `eatRate` of 0.18-0.30 — the per-swing probability the bot declines to defend and 'keeps swinging into the windup' — and the generator's own comment states 'it is where rows 13, 14 and 21 come from'. Rows 13 (swings taken 0.186) and 14 (damage taken 1.098 x max HP) are therefore set by a tuned constant. The commit message's claim that 'every hit taken is a mistimed roll or an unfinished attack' is true of the damage RESOLUTION and false of the DECISION.

The exemplar bot's hold band is 4.0-4.6 m while the generator's own comment three lines above the constant says '2.6-3.2 m is the band where its swing ARRIVES in reach'. The constant and its rationale disagree, and the constant is what runs. A straight-sword R1 reaches 2.1 m, so most of every 76-frame punish window is spent walking, which is why row 27 reads 0.163.

Fight F2 is not a fight. The median distance between player and enemy at the enemy's hitbox-activation frame is 37.06 m and the median minimum distance during the active window is 36.77 m; the enemy swings 46 times at nothing. F2 nonetheless contributed 17 in-band rows to the five-fight median that the piece reports as its headline result. Four of the five fights end at the 9000-frame cap rather than in a kill; only F4 emits a DEATH event.

Poses are instantiated, never blended, at EVERY state boundary. Worst single-frame weapon-socket displacement, over five fights: RUN->ROLL_STARTUP 2.528 m (74 occurrences), SPRINT->ROLL_STARTUP 2.521 m (27), ATK_RECOVER->ATK_STARTUP 2.293 m (65, inside a single chained attack), WALK->ROLL_STARTUP 2.131 m, IDLE->ROLL_STARTUP 1.922 m. That is 115-152 m/s against a declared straight-sword peak tip speed of 18.5 m/s. Within a state the worst jump is 0.818 m. The remediation genuinely fixed the double-applied idle pose and the peak tip speed WITHIN attacks (14 of 14 movesets now at or under the declared column, straight-sword R1 arc 268° against round 1's 615°, per-substep travel 0.41-1.08 capsule radii against 2.90); the transition snap is a different instance of the same defect and it survives.

The recovery arc still exceeds the active arc in 7 of 14 movesets: dagger R1 23° vs 20°, dagger R2 27° vs 23°, straight sword R1 77° vs 71°, straight sword R2 86° vs 81°, halberd R1 79° vs 45°, halberd R2 90° vs 51°, ultra-greatsword R1 93° vs 54°. Recovery in a Souls swing is the blade coming to rest.

A successful parry produces no riposte. cmb-poise m6 shows parried:true at press_lead 18 and 24 with parried_len_f 56 matching spec, and riposted:false with damage:0 in all seven cases. RI-CMB05 M7 is a straight fail and the parry currently has no payoff at all.

Two of the project's own instruments are vacuous and read as passes. cmb-poise m3_heavy returns stagger_lengths_f: [] for both greatsword and ultra-greatsword — no stagger was produced, so the 64 f spec is unverified — and cmb-poise m4_hyperarmour's CONTROL case ('hit outside the HA window') reports hp 620 of 620, i.e. the hit never landed, so the probe cannot distinguish working hyperarmour from none. The control not landing is the biggest gap showing up inside the hyperarmour instrument.

RI-CMB07's canonical fight F1 has row 28 (inputs dropped for insufficient stamina) equal to 0 — an automatic-fail condition in the item's own Scoring section. Its 30 INPUT_DROPPED events are all reason:'not_actionable', not 'no_stamina'. The five-fight median is 4 so the automatic fail does not fire on the reported figure, but the fight designated `canonical_fight` and copied to RI-CMB07-exemplar-frames.jsonl is the one where the bar never denied an input.

Round 1's own instruments, re-run on this commit, are byte-identical for critic-roll.json, critic-iframe.json, critic-frames.json, critic-commit.json, critic-sharp.json, critic-dice.json and critic-geo2.json. The frame layer really is untouched by the remediation and really does still pass. This is the strongest thing in the piece and it should not be lost in the failure.

The exemplar's determinism claim is genuine and was verified rather than trusted: re-running tools/harness/cmb-exemplar.mjs --fights 1 into a scratch directory produced a frames file byte-identical to the shipped RI-CMB07-exemplar-F1-frames.jsonl, and my independent recomputation of all 29 statistics from the raw JSONL reproduced the shipped statistics file exactly. Round 1's failure mode — a statistics file saying one thing and the fight another — does NOT recur.

reports/ is gitignored, so RI-CMB07-exemplar-*.jsonl and the statistics file are not under version control. The piece's single most cited artifact cannot be diffed between waves and would vanish on a clean checkout. It is reproducible from the harness, which is why this is an observation rather than the gap.

gap_closure.acceptance_restated: Rows 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19 and 25 inside their bands over the median of five fights, row 27 an actual number, RI-CMB03 M7's floor (>= 5 of 7) and RI-CMB07 M2's floor (>= 20 of 24) both met.
gap_closure.measured_value: rows 13 = 0.186, 14 = 1.098, 16 = 130, 17 = 0.1406, 18 = 0.3612, 19 = 0.7061, 25 = 373 — all seven in band on the median of five fights, recomputed by this critic from the raw JSONL; row 27 = 0.163, a number but out of band; RI-CMB03 M7 = 7 of 7; RI-CMB07 M2 = 21 of 24 on the build's row set, 20 of 24 if row 9 is restored to the item's own row set, 22 of 26 counting every banded row in §D.
gap_closure.note: The stated acceptance is met on every clause, and the numbers were independently recomputed rather than read from the shipped file. It is recorded as partially-closed rather than closed for three reasons, each measured: the M2 floor is met only at exactly 20 of 24 once row 9 is restored to the denominator the item itself defines; the danger the rows report is produced by a tuned per-swing eatRate constant rather than by the fight; and the underlying disease round 1 diagnosed — the two actors are not in each other's reach — is unchanged, with 141 of 211 enemy swings still resolving as WHIFF and one of the five fights fought at 37 m. The successor gap GAP-W1-enemy-attacks-cannot-reach-contact-range is the mechanical cause and supersedes it in substance.

corpus_extended.note: M2's tunnelling test enumerates 7 PLAYER weapon classes x 24 lateral offsets against a stationary attacker. Nothing in the corpus tests an attacker that TRANSLATES during its own active window, and nothing tests an enemy's attack volume at all. That is why a 1.2-1.6 m hole in every enemy attack survived a full round of critics with M2 passing. Proposed addition, M2b: for every enemy attack declaring root_dz_m > 0, sweep a stationary target from 0.0 m to the attack's outer reach in 0.05 m steps and require a contiguous hit band with no interior gap; report min_hit_distance_m per attack. The instrument already exists as tools/harness/critic-w1-09-r2.mjs --probe reach.

The AP anti-probe table is one-directional in the same way B2 was before B13. AP9 fails damage with no hitbox; nothing fails a hitbox that is active, correctly telegraphed and geometrically unable to reach a target at contact range. Proposed AP10: for every enemy attack, the fraction of active-window frames on which a target inside the attack's declared reach Omega is NOT covered by the swept volume must be 0.

Two defects. (1) The item says 'the 24 rows that carry a band' but §D shows 26 rows with a band entry (every row except 3, 10 and 26), which lets an implementation choose its own denominator; the shipped statistics file un-banded row 9, which it fails 5 of 5, and kept the total at 24. The item must enumerate its banded rows by number. (2) M2 requires the enemy to be governed by RI-AI01-05, which is unsatisfiable until W1-12 ships; the item needs a declared Mode B-prime with its own reduced weight so a half-scripted exchange is scoreable without being scoreable AS Mode B.

Re-filed from round 1 because it bit this round too: the blind pair compares our H[k] vector with one generated from §B, and when the build is exact the two sides are bit-identical, so the pack cannot discriminate. The same holds for RI-CMB02's census and RI-CMB06's M4 table. A blind pair needs a discriminator that varies WITHIN correctness — the shape of the roll's per-frame root-delta curve would do it, and would have caught the 2.53 m transition snap.

arbitration_questions.question: Does an enemy attack that is perfectly telegraphed, perfectly framed and geometrically unable to hit a target at contact range constitute an AR-1 failure? A1 bans a to-hit roll and A4 bans an untelegraphed attack, but nothing in the AR-1 table addresses an attack whose hit volume has a hole. Empirically the champion's moveset behaves like a 1.2-3.6 m distance band, which is the shape AR-1 exists to forbid, and the only thing distinguishing it from a distance check is that the band translates with the attacker's root motion.
arbitration_questions.souls_side: Souls owns hitboxes and hit resolution inside the fight (ARBITRATION §1). A swept capsule with a hole in it is not a Souls hitbox, and 'deterministic hit-or-miss by geometry' is violated in spirit when the geometry cannot reach the target: the player's survival is decided by a band, not by a volume.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: No Morrowind mechanic is involved. The competing reading is simply that this is an ordinary implementation bug rather than a seam violation, and that inflating it to an AR-1 hard fail would cap the piece at 2 for something no doctrine text names.

The escalation ladder was used in full and it is what found the gap: zoom (per-swing rather than per-fight), change the sample (the enemy's attacks rather than the player's), stress it (stand still and mash), second-order (does the i-frame window change how I fight, not does it exist), and first-minute-versus-tenth-hour (a player finds the inner hole in the first minute).

notes: Ordering, per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8: the raw measurements in this verdict were taken before round 1's verdict was consulted for closure. The independent recomputation of RI-CMB07 §D (critic-r2-recompute.mjs) was written from the reference item and reads only reports/w1-09/exemplar/*-frames.jsonl; it never opens RI-CMB07-exemplar-statistics.json. The blind pick for RI-CMB07 was recorded before the reveal file was read. What the remediation genuinely closed, verified by this critic rather than taken on trust: GUARD_BREAK is now exactly 40 f with stamina held at 0.00 throughout (round 1: 46 f with regeneration running at 0.75/frame); the medium stagger is exactly 44 f (round 1: 50 f); jump, two-handing, weapon swap and a non-pausing menu now exist and change state on the press frame (round 1: four inert buttons); peak tip speed within an attack is at or under the declared column on all 14 movesets and the straight-sword R1 arc is 268 degrees (round 1: x2.69 and 615 degrees); per-substep travel is 0.41-1.08 capsule radii (round 1: 2.90), which restores RI-CMB04 §C's substep rationale; RI-CMB03 M7 now passes 7 of 7; and the exemplar is five fights, deterministic, and reproduces byte-for-byte from the current build. That is a large and real body of work. It does not reach the gate because the exemplar is still not Mode B, four of its banded rows are out including one the file silently un-banded, its M3(d) fingerprint does not cluster, poses still snap 2.5 m at every state boundary, a successful parry still produces no riposte, and the enemy cannot hit anything standing next to it.
